newsitem.title: USA: Albert denies charges, will broadcast playoffs.
newsitem.headline: Albert denies charges, will broadcast playoffs.

text.p: Sportcaster Marv Albert Thursday denied allegations that he sexually assaulted a Virginia woman and NBC announced he would broadcast the NBA playoffs as scheduled.

Albert, 53, was charged Monday in Arlington Circuit Court with one felony count of forcible sodomy and one misdemeanor count of assault and battery after the alleged incident in an Arlington, Va., hotel room Feb. 12.

"Marv Albert has vehemently denied all these serious allegations against him," NBC said in a statement. "Prior to these charges being made public Tuesday, Marv at no time was ever afforded any opportunity to discuss the facts with police or prosecuting attorneys."
Albert, one of the most recognisable voices in American sports broadcasting with his trademark "Yesss!", was going to appear in public later Thursday to make his own statement, his spokesman said.

The NBC statement continued, "He is now required to defend himself in a courtroom in the near future. Given these facts, Marv will broadcast the NBA playoffs on NBC continuing this Saturday in Miami."
Game three of the Eastern Conference Finals between the Chicago Bulls and Miami Heat was scheduled to be played in Miami Saturday and broadcast on NBC Sports.

Police said Albert allegedly became enraged with the 41-year-old woman, threw her on the bed, bit her violently on the back 15 times and forced her to perform oral sex. New York newspapers quoted police sources as saying the woman had refused Albert's request to join him for sex with another man.
Forcible sodomy carries a penalty of five years to life in prison and assault and battery is punishable by up to 12 months and a $2,500 fine.
WRC-TV in Washington reported Wednesday that Albert's accuser faced a criminal charge for allegedly threatening to kill her former boyfriend.

Court documents showed the woman had pleaded not guilty to the misdemeanor charge, according to the report. The alleged threats were made in three cellular telephone calls placed to the boyfriend March 13, WRC-TV reported.

Albert also broadcasts for the Madison Square Garden Network in New York, where he is famous as the decades-long commentator for the New York Knicks of the National Basketball Association and the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League.
